=== 1. A FALSE PROOF CLAIM FROM THE PREVIOUS ROUND, AND THE REAL GAP IT HID ===

The previous return claimed: "MUTATION 2 — the door test's per-OS assembly conjunct dropped (IsDoorType = PlatformFactory.IsFactoryType alone): SameNamedDoorInAnotherAssembly_FromContainerFactory_IsReported [FAIL] ... Failed: 1, Passed: 0". That is NOT reproducible. I applied exactly that mutation to exactly that code in an isolated copy:

  private static readonly Func<INamedTypeSymbol, bool> IsDoorType =
      type => PlatformFactory.IsFactoryType(type);

and the named test PASSED, and so did the whole suite: "Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 599, Skipped: 0, Total: 599". The likely explanation is that the previous round's edit also hit the MEMBER half, since both lines carry the same `IsPerOsType(type) &&` conjunct — but the claim as written is false, and I am reporting it rather than quietly restating it.

The gap it hid is real. AG0029's door test has two halves: IsDoorMember (consulted by the call lens) and IsDoorType (consulted by the written-name and declared-type lenses). The wrong-assembly fixture writes the imitation as a CALL — `PlatformServices.Create()` — which trips BOTH lenses at once, and the assertion is Assert.NotEmpty plus all-are-AG0029. Either lens alone satisfies it, so neither half was pinned.

Closed by one added fixture: OneDoorIntoPerOsAnalyzerTests.SameNamedDoorTypeReferenceInAnotherAssembly_InsideContainerFactory_IsReported writes `typeof(PlatformServices)` against the decoy assembly inside Create(). Nothing is called, so only the written-name lens can fire and only IsDoorType can reject it. Mutation 2 now fails it (Assert.NotEmpty, Collection was empty) and mutation 1 fails it too. I judged this inside the confirmed fix rather than beyond it: the direction requires "AG0029's own door test rejects it", and half a door test proved by nothing does not meet that. No rule behavior changed — the analyzer sources are byte-identical to what the previous round submitted; only the test file gained the fixture and one private run helper.

=== 2. AN UNPROVABLE CONJUNCT, RECORDED NOT FIXED ===

AG0029's door MEMBER conjunct cannot be isolated by any fixture, and I verified that rather than assuming it. Mutation 4 — IsDoorMember reduced to `(member, type) => PlatformFactory.Is(member, type)`, the per-OS conjunct dropped — passes the whole suite: "Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 600, Skipped: 0, Total: 600".

Why it is unobservable, from the code: on the Boundaries gate OneDoorRule.InspectCall returns early unless isInScopeFromBoundaries(type), which IS IsPerOsType, so the conjunct is redundant there by construction. On the Engine gate, every way to reach the decoy door member also puts the decoy TYPE in front of a type lens — a static call must qualify with the type name (written-name lens), a using-static or alias writes the name outside Create() (reported for site), and an instance obtained from a call carries the decoy as an invoked-return type (declared-type lens). Each of those is rejected by the intact IsDoorType, so the observable answer never changes.

I did NOT remove it.
